scope: Pauris 3 and 4, exact corpus occurrence binding, all commentary original. Does not update active app lessons.

bibliography.title: Prof Sahib Singh Guru Granth Darpan Ang 2
Guru Nanak Nishkam Sewak Jatha Jap Ji Sahib
Sikh Research and Education Center Japji

units.title: Many descriptions, none the whole
units.spine: The many ways people praise divine power/giving/knowledge/near and far are incomplete; the Giver's generosity and Hukam outlast every single viewpoint.
units.englishArrival: One person notices power, another a gift, another knowledge or presence. The repeated voices invite humility: each view contributes without exhausting the Divine.
units.punjabiArrival: ਕੋਈ ਤਾਕਤ ਨੂੰ, ਕੋਈ ਦਾਤ ਨੂੰ, ਕੋਈ ਗਿਆਨ ਜਾਂ ਨੇੜਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਵੇਖਦਾ ਹੈ। ਹਰ ਬਿਆਨ ਕੁਝ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਕੋਈ ਇਕੱਲਾ ਸਾਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸ ਸਕਦਾ।
units.theTurn: After multiplying examples of what people say, the pauri concludes with the endless giving and a Hukam beyond any one speaker's account.
units.connection: Pauri 2 Hukam; Pauri 4 the Giver and what offering is possible; review any separate SGGS connections in full context.
units.reflection: When are you tempted to treat one experience or explanation as the whole? Can gratitude coexist with intellectual humility?
units.teachBack: Name three distinct kinds of praise in the first eight lines and explain why the final lines discourage a complete human account.

units.title: Beyond bargains: what offering, what words?
units.spine: The sovereign Giver receives endless requests. The stanza asks what true offering and speech look like, turning toward Divine Name, remembrance, grace and the True One.
units.englishArrival: When everything is already a gift, what could a person place before the Giver? The questions of an offering and spoken words move the pauri from transaction toward reflection and grace.
units.punjabiArrival: ਜਦੋਂ ਸਭ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਹਨ, ਤਾਂ ਅਸੀਂ ਉਸ ਅੱਗੇ ਕੀ ਰੱਖ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਾਂ? ਪਉੜੀ ਭੇਟ ਅਤੇ ਬੋਲਣ ਦੇ ਸਵਾਲ ਤੋਂ ਸੱਚੇ ਨਾਮ, ਵਿਚਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਵੱਲ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

vocabulary.en: contested contextual rendering: Name or justice/order
auspicious early period / time for awakening and reflection

units.theTurn: The human questions shift from asking and offering toward remembrance and the recognition that the True One is the source.
units.connection: Pauri 3 ending on giving and Hukam, Pauri 5 on the nature of the One; compare other Ang references only after human review.
units.reflection: When does gratitude become a bargain? Can you contemplate something meaningful without treating attention as a transaction?
units.teachBack: What are the two questions about offering and speech, and how does Amrit Vela change the direction of the stanza?

lines.simpleEn: People praise Divine power or strength, each from their own understanding.
lines.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਦੀ ਤਾਕਤ ਦਾ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਆਪਣੀ ਸਮਝ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ।
lines.study: The repeated ‘ਗਾਵੈ ਕੋ’ is a poetic pattern of different voices. Do not turn this into a claim that political or physical power makes someone closer to God.

lines.simpleEn: Some praise the gifts they have received and recognize a sign of giving.
lines.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਮਿਲੀ ਦਾਤ ਨੂੰ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਦੀ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨੀ ਮੰਨ ਕੇ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: This is the vocabulary of gift and gratitude. The experience of one gift cannot account for the whole Divine nature.

lines.simpleEn: Some praise beautiful virtues and greatness.
lines.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਸੋਹਣੇ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਵਡਿਆਈਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰ ਕੇ ਗਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: Attention shifts from what a person has received to qualities worthy of praise. ‘ਚਾਰ’ in this context is glossed as beautiful by commentators; verify the historical grammar.

lines.simpleEn: Some speak of difficult knowledge and deep reflection.
lines.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਔਖੀ ਵਿਦਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਡੂੰਘੇ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: Knowledge is one approach to praise, but the stanza's diversity cautions against making any single intellectual description the entirety of truth.

lines.simpleEn: Some describe the creating of the body and its return to dust.
lines.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਸਰੀਰ ਦੀ ਸਿਰਜਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਮਿੱਟੀ ਹੋ ਜਾਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: Creation and mortality appear together. This is devotional poetry about transience, not a laboratory description of cells or matter.

lines.simpleEn: Some describe the giving and taking of life.
lines.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਜੀਵਨ ਲੈਣ ਅਤੇ ਫਿਰ ਦੇਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: The line belongs with the preceding creation/dissolution image; avoid inferring a medical or biological doctrine from its wording.

lines.simpleEn: To some, the Divine appears far away.
lines.simplePa: ਕਿਸੇ ਨੂੰ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਦੂਰ ਜਾਪਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: The stanza now turns from descriptions of power to the person's perception of nearness. This line is one attributed vantage, not an endorsement that the Divine is absent.

lines.simpleEn: To others, the Divine is seen as near and present.
lines.simplePa: ਕਿਸੇ ਨੂੰ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਹਾਜ਼ਰ-ਨਾਜ਼ਰ, ਨੇੜੇ ਦਿੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: Place the near and far lines side by side. Opposed human experiences do not force Guru Nanak to make two contradictory Divine assertions.

lines.simpleEn: There is no end to speaking of these qualities.
lines.simplePa: ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਕਹਿਣ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਅੰਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ।
lines.study: The culmination begins: all human descriptions are partial. Do not present uncertainty here as mere refusal to think; it opens humility.

lines.simpleEn: Countless voices have spoken again and again.
lines.simplePa: ਅਣਗਿਣਤ ਲੋਕ ਵਾਰ-ਵਾਰ ਗੱਲ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਆਏ ਹਨ।
lines.study: Repetition does not yield an exhaustive account. The many voices may deepen appreciation without possessing the whole.

lines.simpleEn: The Giver keeps giving while receivers grow weary.
lines.simplePa: ਦਾਤਾਰ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਲੈਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਥੱਕ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ।
lines.study: The imbalance between giving and receiving evokes abundance; it is not a promise that any requested possession will materialize.

lines.simpleEn: Across ages, beings continue to receive and partake.
lines.simplePa: ਜੁਗਾਂ-ਜੁਗਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਜੀਵ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਤੇ ਵਰਤਦੇ ਆ ਰਹੇ ਹਨ।
lines.study: The temporal scope broadens. What one person experiences in a lifetime is only a partial vantage.

lines.simpleEn: The Divine Hukam directs the path and course of what unfolds.
lines.simplePa: ਹੁਕਮ ਦੇ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਰਾਹ ਚੱਲਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: Connect to Pauri 2: the multiplying descriptions still meet the mystery and breadth of Hukam. Avoid mechanistic fatalism.

lines.simpleEn: Nanak speaks of the carefree Divine flourishing.
lines.simplePa: ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਬੇਪਰਵਾਹ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਦੀ ਖਿੜੀ ਹੋਈ ਅਵਸਥਾ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ।
lines.study: ‘ਵੇਪਰਵਾਹੁ’ should not be taught as a human license for indifference to others; this is a Divine depiction whose poetry needs qualified interpretation.

lines.simpleEn: The True Sovereign endures; the Name/order and language of love require careful interpretation.
lines.simplePa: ਸਦਾ-ਥਿਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਹੈ; 'ਸਾਚੁ ਨਾਇ' ਅਤੇ ਅਪਾਰ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਦੀ ਵਿਆਖਿਆ ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਕਰਨੀ ਹੈ।
lines.study: Professor Sahib Singh reads ਨਾਇ through ਨਿਆਇ, Divine justice/order, with grammatical argument; other translations emphasize Divine Name. The short meaning must disclose this rather than resolve it by AI fiat.

lines.simpleEn: People repeatedly ask for gifts; the Giver gives.
lines.simplePa: ਲੋਕ ਵਾਰ-ਵਾਰ ਦਾਤ ਮੰਗਦੇ ਹਨ, ਤੇ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਦਾਤਾਂ ਦੇਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
lines.study: Notice the repeated request before the next question. The pauri is not merely a guarantee that material petitions are always granted.

lines.simpleEn: What offering could we place before the Divine court?
lines.simplePa: ਫਿਰ ਦਰਬਾਰ ਵਿਚ ਕੀ ਭੇਟ ਰੱਖੀਏ ਕਿ ਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਹੋਣ?
lines.study: The image of a court recalls approaching a sovereign with an offering. Guru Nanak turns the reader's assumption about giving and receiving into a question.

lines.simpleEn: What words could we speak so that love is received?
lines.simplePa: ਮੂੰਹੋਂ ਕਿਹੜਾ ਬੋਲ ਬੋਲੀਏ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਸੁਣ ਕੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਮਿਲੇ?
lines.study: This continues the sincere question, not a technique promising that repeating a particular phrase mechanically earns favor.

lines.simpleEn: In Amrit Vela, contemplate the True Name and Divine greatness.
lines.simplePa: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੇ ਸੱਚੇ ਨਾਮ ਅਤੇ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਦਾ ਵੀਚਾਰ ਕਰੀਏ।
lines.study: Sikh tradition commonly associates Amrit Vela with the early hours. Darpan also explains conditions favorable to inward attention; no spiritual stopwatch follows from the line alone.

lines.simpleEn: Garment and liberation language invokes deeds/grace and the Divine glance.
lines.simplePa: ਕਰਮੀ ਕਪੜਾ ਅਤੇ ਨਦਰ ਨਾਲ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦੇ ਦਰ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।
lines.study: This difficult metaphor should be reviewed against original morphology and named scholarship before a literal interpretation is fixed; keep grace and the Divine glance visible.

lines.simpleEn: Nanak says the True One is truly so, by the One's own reality.
lines.simplePa: ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀ ਅਖੀਰ ਵਿਚ ਅਕਾਲ ਪੁਰਖ ਦੀ ਸੱਚੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ।
lines.study: Pauri 4 closes by shifting attention from ‘what can I offer?’ toward the True One. Full theological nuance requires qualified Punjabi/Gurbani review.

editorialRules: Original Gurmukhi text from immutable corpus only
Every summary is original and pending human review
Where Naai/Likhi interpretations differ, cite by named tradition
Do not convert liturgical language into psychiatric diagnosis or physiology
